title: Abdominal Injuries: Hidden Bleeding and What the PCP Adds

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already control bleeding, cover an evisceration, stabilize impaled objects and bind the pelvis. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Know which organs bleed, which spill, and where injuries hide
  2. Assess the abdomen like a PCP: why normal vital signs lie
  3. Know what the PCP adds in the BC Abdominal Injuries protocol

Textbook: Chapter 27, PDF pages 2232–2276
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter twenty-seven: abdominal injuries. As EMRs, you already control external bleeding, cover an evisceration with a moist dressing, stabilize impaled objects, bind the pelvis, and move fast. The hard part of abdominal trauma is that the worst bleeding is hidden. You can't see it, and you can't stop it with your hands. So as a PCP, your value is suspicion and good decisions: knowing which organs bleed, reading the clues early, and using your new tools, the IV, fluids, and TXA, without slowing transport.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第二十七章：腹部创伤。作为 EMR，你们已经会控制外出血、用湿敷料盖住脱出的脏器、固定刺入物、绑骨盆，并且快速转运。腹部创伤难就难在最严重的出血是藏起来的：看不见，也没法用手压住。所以作为 PCP，你的价值在于怀疑和正确决策：知道哪些器官会出血，早早读出线索，并且在不拖慢转运的前提下用好新工具——静脉通路、补液和 TXA。

slides.title: Where the abdomen really is
slides.body:
The abdomen starts at the nipple line

Peritonealliver, spleen, stomach, bowelbleeding or spillage
Retroperitonealaorta, vena cava, pancreas, kidneysfew signs, late
Pelvicbladder, rectum, pelvic vesselsbleeds with pelvic fractures

The diaphragm rises to about the 4th intercostal space: a wound at or below the nipples can enter the abdomen.
slides.say: First, where is the abdomen? Higher than most people think. The diaphragm is dome-shaped and rises to about the fourth intercostal space, roughly the nipple line. So a stab wound to the lower chest can also cut the liver or spleen. Treat any wound at or below the nipples as an abdominal wound too. Inside there are three spaces. The peritoneal space holds the liver, spleen, stomach, and bowel. Behind it, the retroperitoneal space holds the aorta, vena cava, pancreas, and kidneys. And the pelvis holds the bladder, rectum, and many blood vessels.
slides.sayZh: 先问：腹部在哪里？比多数人想的要高。膈肌呈穹顶状，最高可到第四肋间，大约在乳头线。所以下胸部的刀伤也可能伤到肝或脾。凡是乳头线及以下的伤口，都要同时当作腹部伤。腹内分三个区：腹膜腔装着肝、脾、胃和肠；它后面的腹膜后间隙有主动脉、下腔静脉、胰腺和肾；骨盆里有膀胱、直肠和大量血管。

slides.title: Solid organs bleed, hollow organs spill
slides.body:
Solid organsHollow organs
Examplesliver, spleen, pancreas, kidneysstomach, intestines, bladder
Main dangerbleeding → shockspillage → peritonitis
Timingbleeding can be massivestomach: fairly fast; bowel: hours to days

Blunt: spleen about 50%, liver about 30%. Penetrating: liver most often.
slides.say: A simple way to organize abdominal injuries: solid organs bleed, hollow organs spill. The liver, spleen, pancreas, and kidneys are solid and full of blood, so their danger is hemorrhage and shock. The stomach, intestines, and bladder are hollow. When they burst, acid, bacteria, or urine leak out and inflame the lining of the abdomen. That's peritonitis. Stomach acid irritates fairly quickly, but bowel injuries may take hours or days to show. In blunt trauma, the spleen is injured most, in about half of cases, then the liver. In penetrating trauma, the liver is hit most, because it's the biggest.
slides.sayZh: 整理腹部伤有个简单办法：实质器官出血，空腔器官外漏。肝、脾、胰、肾是实质器官，血供丰富，危险是大出血和休克。胃、肠、膀胱是空腔器官，破裂时胃酸、细菌或尿液漏出来，刺激腹膜发炎，这就是腹膜炎。胃酸刺激比较快，肠道损伤可能要几小时甚至几天才表现出来。钝性伤里最常受伤的是脾，约占一半，其次是肝。穿透伤里最常伤到的是肝，因为它最大。

slides.title: How the force does the damage
slides.body:
• Shear: sudden stop; organs tear at their attachments
  • Crush: squeezed between wall and spine; solid organs
  • Compression: belt or air bag spikes pressure; bowel, diaphragm
  • Seat belt sign on the lower belly → usually injury inside
  • Gunshot: deeper and less predictable than a stab
  • Lower rib fractures → think spleen or liver
slides.say: Blunt force injures the abdomen in three ways. Shear: in a sudden stop, organs keep moving and tear where they're attached. The book calls it the third collision: the car hits the wall, the body hits the wheel, and the organs hit the inside of the rib cage. Crush: organs are squeezed between the front wall and the spine; solid organs suffer most. Compression: a lap belt or air bag suddenly raises the pressure, and the bowel or diaphragm can burst. A bruise across the lower abdomen from the belt, the seat belt sign, usually means injury inside. Gunshots are deeper and less predictable than stabs. And lower rib fractures should make you think of the spleen or liver.
slides.sayZh: 钝性力伤腹部有三种方式。剪切：突然停下时，器官还在往前冲，在固定点撕裂。书里叫它「第三次碰撞」：车撞墙，人撞方向盘，器官撞到肋骨和胸壁内侧。挤压：器官被夹在前腹壁和脊柱之间，实质器官受害最重。压缩：腰带或气囊让腹压骤升，肠或膈肌可能被撑破。下腹部一条安全带勒出的瘀伤，也就是安全带征，通常意味着腹内有伤。枪伤比刀伤更深、更难预测。下位肋骨骨折，要想到脾或肝。

slides.q: A snowboarder fell onto a rail on his left side. He has pain over his left lower ribs and, oddly, in his left shoulder. HR 108, BP 126/80. What should worry you most?
options: A shoulder sprain from the fall
A spleen injury, with shoulder pain referred from the diaphragm
A pancreas injury, because the pain is spreading
Nothing serious, because his blood pressure is normal
slides.say: Let's check. A snowboarder fell onto a rail on his left side. He has pain over his left lower ribs and, oddly, in his left shoulder. Heart rate one hundred eight, blood pressure one twenty-six over eighty. What should worry you most? A, a shoulder sprain from the fall. B, a spleen injury, with shoulder pain referred from the diaphragm. C, a pancreas injury, because the pain is spreading. D, nothing serious, because his blood pressure is normal. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 考考你。一名单板滑雪者左侧身体摔在铁杆上，左下肋疼痛，奇怪的是左肩也痛。心率一百零八，血压一百二十六比八十。你最该担心什么？A 摔倒导致的肩部扭伤；B 脾损伤，肩痛是膈肌受刺激引起的牵涉痛；C 胰腺损伤，因为疼痛在扩散；D 没什么大事，因为血压正常。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Left lower rib injuries go with spleen injuries, and blood irritating the diaphragm can be felt in the left shoulder; that's called Kehr sign. A ignores a mechanism right over the spleen. C is less likely: pancreatic pain is usually in the upper middle abdomen and goes to the back, often hours later. D is wrong because a normal blood pressure doesn't rule out internal bleeding, and his heart rate is already up.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。左下肋损伤常伴脾损伤，血液刺激膈肌，可以在左肩感到疼痛，这叫 Kehr 征。A 忽略了正好作用在脾上的受伤机制。C 可能性较小：胰腺痛通常在上腹正中、放射到背部，而且常常几小时后才出现。D 错，血压正常不能排除内出血，何况他的心率已经升高了。

slides.title: Organs that hide their injury
slides.body:
OrganClue
Liverright lower chest or RUQ hit; big bleed plus bile
Spleenleft lower ribs; left shoulder pain; up to 40% no symptoms
Pancreas, duodenumwheel or handlebar; pain to the back, hours to days later
Diaphragmside impact; breathing trouble, absent breath sounds
Bladderpelvic fracture, full bladder; blood in urine
slides.say: Some organs hide their injuries well. The liver reaches up to the nipples, so right lower chest trauma can tear it; it bleeds heavily and leaks bile. The spleen sits under the left lower ribs. Up to forty percent of patients with a splenic injury have no symptoms, and an enlarged spleen, for example from mono, can rupture after minor contact. The pancreas and duodenum sit deep and far back. Think of them after a steering wheel or handlebar to the upper belly; pain into the back may appear only hours or days later. A torn diaphragm can cause breathing trouble. And a full bladder ruptures more easily, often with a pelvic fracture.
slides.sayZh: 有些器官很会藏伤。肝的上缘可高达乳头，所以右下胸外伤可能撕裂肝脏，出血多，还会漏胆汁。脾在左下肋下面，脾损伤的病人多达百分之四十没有症状；脾肿大时，比如得了单核细胞增多症，轻微碰撞就可能破裂。胰腺和十二指肠位置深、靠后，上腹部被方向盘或车把撞过后要想到它们，放射到背部的疼痛可能几小时甚至几天后才出现。膈肌撕裂可以导致呼吸困难。膀胱越满越容易破，常伴骨盆骨折。

slides.title: The retroperitoneum: quiet bleeding
slides.body:
Blood behind the abdomen gives few signs

  • Often little pain, no rigidity, no distention
  • Grey Turner sign (flanks), Cullen sign (around the navel)
  • Both appear 12–24 hours later: absent on scene means nothing
  • Ultrasound can't see retroperitoneal bleeding
  • Trauma can worsen an existing aortic aneurysm
slides.say: The retroperitoneum is the space behind the abdominal lining, and bleeding there is quiet. The blood is held in place, so the patient may have little pain, no rigidity, and no swelling. Two bruising patterns are classic: Grey Turner sign on the flanks, and Cullen sign around the navel. But both usually appear twelve to twenty-four hours after the injury, so their absence on scene tells you nothing. Even a prehospital ultrasound can't see retroperitoneal bleeding. And in older patients, remember that trauma can make an existing abdominal aortic aneurysm worse.
slides.sayZh: 腹膜后间隙在腹膜衬里的后面，那里的出血很「安静」。血被局限住，病人可能不怎么痛，没有肌紧张，也不胀。有两种经典的瘀斑：侧腹部的 Grey Turner 征和脐周的 Cullen 征。但两者通常在伤后十二到二十四小时才出现，所以现场看不到，什么也说明不了。连院前超声也看不到腹膜后出血。对老年人，还要记得外伤会让原有的腹主动脉瘤加重。

slides.title: Why normal vital signs lie
slides.body:
A normal BP and a soft belly don't clear the abdomen

  • About 20% with major abdominal bleeding have a normal first exam
  • Low BP, fast pulse, confusion may wait until > 40% blood loss
  • Distention is late; peritonitis can take hours to days
  • Beta-blockers hide a fast pulse; old and young compensate poorly
  • The quiet patient with knees drawn up may be the sickest
  • Shock out of proportion to what you see → think abdomen
slides.say: This is the key idea of the chapter: a normal blood pressure and a soft belly don't clear the abdomen. About twenty percent of patients with major bleeding into the abdomen have a normal first exam. Hypotension, a fast pulse, and confusion may not appear until more than forty percent of the blood volume is lost. Distention is a late sign, and peritonitis can take hours to days. Beta-blockers stop the heart rate from rising, and very young and old patients compensate poorly. A patient lying very still with knees drawn up may be sicker than one rolling around. And shock out of proportion to the visible injuries means think abdomen.
slides.sayZh: 这是本章的关键：血压正常、肚子软，都不能排除腹部损伤。腹腔内大量出血的病人，约百分之二十第一次检查是正常的。低血压、心跳快、意识混乱，可能要到失血超过百分之四十才出现。腹胀是晚期征象，腹膜炎可能要几小时到几天才出现。β 受体阻滞剂让心率升不起来，太小和太老的病人代偿能力都差。静静躺着、屈着膝的病人，可能比来回打滚的人伤得更重。休克程度和看得见的伤不相称时，要想到腹部。

slides.title: Your PCP abdominal exam
slides.body:
1. Expose and inspect: bruises, abrasions, seat belt sign
  2. Gently palpate all four quadrants: tenderness, guarding, rigidity
  3. Skip bowel sounds: too slow, too noisy
  4. Check the back and skin folds for wounds
  5. Repeat the exam en route; trend the vital signs

Document: seat belt use and position, pain, nausea, abdominal shape, findings, alcohol or drugs.
slides.say: As a PCP, your exam goes deeper, and you repeat it. Expose the abdomen and look for bruises, abrasions, and the seat belt sign. Gently palpate all four quadrants, watching the face for tenderness, guarding, and rigidity. Skip bowel sounds; they take minutes to hear properly, and scenes are noisy. Always check the back and skin folds; wounds hide there. Then repeat the exam during transport, because serial exams often catch a worsening abdomen before the vital signs change. And don't let the chief complaint distract you: a patient may only talk about a painful wrist while bleeding inside. Document seat belt use, pain, nausea, the abdomen's shape, and every finding.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你的检查要更深入，而且要反复做。暴露腹部，查看瘀伤、擦伤和安全带征。轻轻触诊四个象限，看着病人的脸，找压痛、护腹和肌紧张。肠鸣音就别听了：要听好几分钟才准，现场又吵。一定要查背部和皮肤皱褶，伤口会藏在那里。然后在转运途中重复检查，因为连续检查常常能在生命体征变化之前发现腹部在恶化。也别被主诉带偏：病人可能只说手腕痛，肚子里却在出血。要记录安全带使用情况、疼痛、恶心、腹部外形，以及每一项发现。

slides.q: A 35-year-old driver, 30 minutes after a crash, has a seat belt bruise across the lower abdomen. HR 124, BP 84/56, skin cool and pale. No head injury. Transport is 20 minutes. You are the PCP. What is the best plan?
options: Start an IV and give 2 L on scene, then move him
Load and go; en route: IV, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L reassessing every 500 mL, and consider TXA
Give no fluids: only surgery can stop internal bleeding
Hold TXA until the hospital confirms the bleeding
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A thirty-five-year-old driver, thirty minutes after a crash, has a seat belt bruise across the lower abdomen. Heart rate one hundred twenty-four, blood pressure eighty-four over fifty-six, skin cool and pale. No head injury. Transport is twenty minutes. What is the best plan? A, start an IV and give two litres on scene, then move him. B, load and go; en route, an IV, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres reassessing every five hundred, and consider TXA. C, give no fluids, because only surgery can stop internal bleeding. D, hold TXA until the hospital confirms the bleeding. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名三十五岁司机，车祸后三十分钟，下腹部有一条安全带瘀伤。心率一百二十四，血压八十四比五十六，皮肤湿冷苍白。没有颅脑外伤。转运时间二十分钟。最好的方案是什么？A 在现场开静脉、输两升液体，再搬动他；B 立即装车出发，途中开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评，并考虑 TXA；C 不补液，因为只有手术才能止住内出血；D 等医院确认出血后再给 TXA。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The BC Abdominal Injuries protocol puts vascular access and correcting hypoperfusion en route, and the hypovolemia protocol gives twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. He's in shock from likely hidden bleeding, within three hours of injury, an adult, without a head injury, so TXA fits. A wastes scene time and skips reassessment. C is half true: surgery is the real fix, but fluids are the bridge. D delays a drug with a three-hour limit.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 腹部创伤流程把开静脉通路和纠正低灌注放在途中，低血容量流程的剂量是每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评。他很可能因隐匿出血而休克，受伤不到三小时，是成人，没有颅脑外伤，所以符合 TXA 的条件。A 浪费现场时间，也没有复评。C 只对了一半：手术才是根本，但补液是撑到手术的桥梁。D 拖延了一种有三小时时限的药。

slides.title: Pelvic fractures: the ring
slides.body:
TypeCausePelvic volume
Open bookfront-to-back (head-on)bigger → big bleed
Lateral compressionside impactsmaller; usually stable
Vertical shearfall from heightbigger; unstable

Broken pelvis = multisystem trauma until proven otherwise. Bind before transport (BC binder rules).
slides.say: The pelvis is a ring of bones held by strong ligaments, so breaking it takes great force. That's why a pelvic fracture means multisystem trauma until proven otherwise, often with bladder, urethra, abdominal, chest, or head injuries. The type matters. An open-book fracture, from a head-on impact, spreads the ring and makes the pelvis bigger, so it can hold a huge bleed, and the patient may stay hypotensive despite fluids. A side impact usually squeezes the ring smaller and is often stable. A vertical shear, from a fall, is unstable and bigger. Use the BC binder rules from Chapter twenty-one, and bind before transport.
slides.sayZh: 骨盆是一圈骨头，由强韧的韧带连在一起，要很大的力才能打断。所以骨盆骨折在排除之前都要当作多系统创伤，常伴膀胱、尿道、腹部、胸部或头部损伤。类型很重要。开书样骨折来自正面撞击，骨盆环被撑开、容积变大，能藏下大量出血，病人补液后可能仍然低血压。侧面撞击通常把骨盆挤小，多半稳定。垂直剪切来自高处坠落，不稳定、容积变大。按第二十一章讲的 BC 骨盆固定规则，转运前绑好骨盆。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: Abdominal Injuries protocol
slides.body:
BC Abdominal Injuries protocol (fluid dose from the Hypovolemia protocol)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control external hemorrhage
  • Limit movement to protect clots
  • Protect against heat loss
  • Evisceration: moist sterile dressing + occlusive layer
  • Don't put organs back; position of comfort
  • Transport

PCP adds (en route)

  • Vascular access
  • Correct hypoperfusion: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL
  • TXA, if indicated
slides.say: Here's the BC Abdominal Injuries protocol. Every licence level controls external bleeding, limits patient movement so clots aren't disturbed, protects against heat loss, and covers eviscerated organs with a moist sterile dressing and an occlusive layer, without pushing them back. Then position of comfort, and transport. The PCP column is short, but powerful. En route, you obtain vascular access and correct hypoperfusion, using the hypovolemia protocol's dose: twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. And you give TXA, tranexamic acid, if indicated. Notice the words en route: none of this costs scene time.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的腹部创伤流程。所有执照级别都要：控制外出血；减少搬动，以免冲掉血凝块；防止热量流失；脱出的脏器用湿的无菌敷料加一层封闭层盖好，不塞回去；然后取舒适体位、转运。PCP 这一栏很短，但很有分量。在途中，你开静脉通路并纠正低灌注，剂量用低血容量流程的：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评。有指征时，给 TXA，也就是氨甲环酸。注意「途中」两个字：这些都不占用现场时间。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Book: scene time 10 min or less; the IV goes in en route
  • Book: no head injury → systolic 80–90, not a normal BP
  • Head injury too? BC wants systolic > 120
  • TXA: 2 g IV over 1 min; not > 3 h, < 12 y, isolated TBI
  • Beta-blockers hide tachycardia: ask about medications
  • Methoxyflurane only if stable; no opioids on the BC exam
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs. Internal bleeding only stops in the operating room, so the book asks for scene times of ten minutes or less, and your IV goes in en route. More fluid isn't better: the book aims for a systolic of eighty to ninety when there's no head injury, not a normal pressure, and BC gives the bolus in steps, reassessing every five hundred millilitres. But with a head injury, BC wants a systolic above one hundred twenty. TXA is two grams by IV push over one minute, and never after three hours, under age twelve, or for an isolated head injury. Ask about beta-blockers. And for pain, methoxyflurane is only for stable patients.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 要注意的事。内出血只有手术室能止住，所以书上要求现场时间在十分钟以内，静脉在途中开。补液不是越多越好：书上说没有颅脑外伤时，目标收缩压是八十到九十，不是正常血压；BC 则是分步补液，每五百毫升复评一次。但合并颅脑外伤时，BC 要求收缩压高于一百二十。TXA 是两克静脉推注、一分钟推完；受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁、单纯颅脑外伤都绝不能给。要问有没有吃 β 受体阻滞剂。镇痛方面，甲氧氟烷只用于稳定的病人。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Never pack abdominal wounds (BC Wound Care)
  • Evisceration: BC adds an occlusive layer over the moist dressing
  • Binder: centre on the greater trochanters (book: iliac crests)
  • Book: systolic 80–90 → BC: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Head injury: BC systolic > 120
  • EMRs have no IV; no opioids on the EMR or PCP exam
slides.say: Let's line up the book and BC. BC's Wound Care protocol says never pack wounds of the abdomen, chest, or neck. For an evisceration, the book uses a saline-soaked dressing; BC adds an occlusive layer over the moist sterile dressing. For the pelvis, the book ties a sheet at the level of the iliac crests; BC centres the binder on the greater trochanters. The book's fluid goal is a systolic of eighty to ninety; BC's dose is twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. With a head injury, BC wants a systolic over one hundred twenty. And EMRs have no IV access, and opioids aren't on the EMR or PCP licensing exam, though BCEHS PCPs may give them after added-scope training.
slides.sayZh: 把这一章书和 BC 的不同对一下。BC 伤口处理流程规定：腹部、胸部、颈部的伤口绝不填塞。脏器脱出，书上用生理盐水浸湿的敷料；BC 要求在湿的无菌敷料外面再加一层封闭层。骨盆固定，书上把床单绑在髂嵴水平；BC 要求固定带中心对准股骨大转子。书上的补液目标是收缩压八十到九十；BC 的剂量是每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次。合并颅脑外伤时，BC 要求收缩压高于一百二十。另外，EMR 没有静脉通路权限，EMR 和 PCP 的执照考试都不考阿片类药物；BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后可以用。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Abdomen starts at the nipple line; solid organs bleed, hollow ones spill
  2. Normal vitals don't clear it: trust the mechanism, repeat the exam
  3. PCP adds en route: IV, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L (every 500 mL), TXA if indicated

Next: Chapter 28, Musculoskeletal Injuries
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: the abdomen starts at the nipple line, and solid organs bleed while hollow organs spill. Two: normal vital signs and a soft belly don't clear the abdomen. Let the mechanism drive your suspicion, and repeat your exam during transport. Three: the PCP adds vascular access, fluids at twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres with reassessment every five hundred, and TXA if indicated, all en route, because the real treatment is in the operating room. Next, Chapter twenty-eight: musculoskeletal injuries. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，腹部从乳头线开始；实质器官出血，空腔器官外漏。二，生命体征正常、肚子软，都不能排除腹部伤；让受伤机制决定你的怀疑程度，并在途中反复检查。三，PCP 多做的是：开静脉通路、按每公斤二十毫升最多两升补液、每五百毫升复评，有指征时给 TXA，全部在途中做，因为真正的治疗在手术室。下一章是第二十八章：肌肉骨骼损伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
